summary: the rows of kheap_hosttest.c that size the heap, give it a region past the floor and keep the cache's pages at the region's top, with five faults in a private copy of rach2/sys/mm/kheap.c, each of which must fail the checks named for it and no other; the test includes kheap.c by a path relative to itself, so the build copies the test, tests/host/compat and rach2/sys under the work directory

argv: set -e; rm -rf ${WORK}/b; mkdir -p ${WORK}/b/rach2 ${WORK}/b/tests/host; cp -R rach2/sys ${WORK}/b/rach2/; cp ${SRC}/rach2/sys/mm/kheap.c ${WORK}/b/rach2/sys/mm/kheap.c; cp tests/host/kheap_hosttest.c ${WORK}/b/tests/host/; cp -R tests/host/compat ${WORK}/b/tests/host/; deps=$(grep -oE 'host-deps:[^*]*' tests/host/kheap_hosttest.c | sed 's/host-deps://' | tr '\n' ' '); cd ${WORK}/b; ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 -DRACH2_HOSTTEST -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -g -O1 -Wno-empty-body -ffreestanding -I rach2/sys -I rach2/sys/arch/x86 -I rach2/sys/arch/i686 -I rach2/sys/lib -I rach2/sys/proc -I tests/host/compat -o ${WORK}/kheap_hosttest tests/host/kheap_hosttest.c $deps

faults.name: no-floor
faults.summary: gives a small machine an eighth of its memory, under 256 MiB

lines: FAIL: x86-64, under 2 GiB: the floor

faults.name: a-quarter
faults.summary: gives the heap a quarter of the memory instead of an eighth

lines: FAIL: x86-64, under 2 GiB: the floor
FAIL: x86-64, QEMU's 8 GiB: an eighth in grains of 4 MiB
FAIL: x86-64, just under 4 TiB: an eighth, under the cap

faults.name: no-cap
faults.summary: lets the heap pass the region the layout has

lines: FAIL: a region under the floor: the region

faults.name: short-map
faults.summary: sizes the page map of a large region for a quarter of its pages, so the map's last pages are given out as the heap's

lines: FAIL: of three pages, a frame each, for 66560 pages
FAIL: and held by the heap, with nothing in use
FAIL: the first page given is after the map
FAIL: every page below the reserve but the map's is one run
FAIL: and every frame but the map's went back

faults.name: one-end
faults.summary: takes the cache's pages from the bottom with the rest, so their holes break every run

lines: FAIL: with the single pages given back, a run of 17 lies below every cache page
FAIL: a page the cache gives back is the next cache page
